title: Electoral votes per US state (Data panel), 2024 and 2028 elections
publisher: U.S. Census Bureau, 2020 Census apportionment of the U.S. House of Representatives
note: Bundled with the editor, not fetched. A state's electors are its seats in the House plus its two senators; the District of Columbia has 3 (23rd Amendment). Maine and Nebraska split their votes by congressional district; the map shows each state's total.
credit: U.S. Census Bureau, 2020 Census apportionment; electors = House seats + 2 (the District of Columbia has 3). Public domain.

verified.file: apportionment-2020-table01.xlsx (Table 1, apportionment population and number of representatives by state)
verified.rule: That electors are the House seats plus two senators, with 3 for the District of Columbia and 538 in all, is confirmed by https://www.usa.gov/electoral-college. The National Archives page on the allocation could not be reached from the machine used to check, so the per-state electoral counts are the Census seats plus 2 and have no second per-state source.
verified.years: The 2020 apportionment gives the electors for the 2024 and 2028 presidential elections; the 2030 census apportionment applies from 2032.
